# The Lab

> The Lab (https://lab.ethpandaops.io) is ethPandaOps' Ethereum network analytics site. Its pages are a client-side app, so fetching a page URL returns no data. Every number on the site comes from a public, read-only HTTP API on the same host, with no key.

The API describes itself. Use these endpoints to find what data exists, what each field means and how to query it.

## Discover

- [Networks](https://lab.ethpandaops.io/api/v1/config): JSON listing every network the API serves (`networks[].name`) with its genesis time and fork schedule. Use the name as `{network}` below.
- [Tables](https://lab.ethpandaops.io/api/v1/mainnet/tables): JSON at `/api/v1/{network}/tables` listing every table with its description, its endpoint (`path`), its `primary_key` fields and its coverage (`bounds`). Start here.
- Table detail: JSON at `/api/v1/{network}/tables/{table}` giving each field's type and description, the filter operators each field accepts (`filters`), and the endpoint's other parameters, such as paging and order.
- [OpenAPI spec](https://lab.ethpandaops.io/api/v1/mainnet/openapi.yaml): the exhaustive reference, an OpenAPI 3 YAML spec per network at `/api/v1/{network}/openapi.yaml`, from which the two endpoints above are built. It is around 10 MB; download it once and search it rather than reading it whole.

`bounds` gives the `min` and `max` processed position of a table. A position is a unix timestamp or a block number, depending on the table. Data outside that range has not been processed yet, which is not the same as it not having happened.

## Query

- Each table's endpoint is `GET /api/v1/{network}/{table}`, the `path` in the table list. It returns JSON with the rows in an array named after the table.
- Filters are query parameters named `<field>_<operator>`, using the operators in the field's `filters`. `in_values` and `not_in_values` take comma-separated lists.
- Send at least one filter on a `primary_key` field, or the API answers `{"code":3,"message":"primary key field <field> is required"}`.
- `page_size`, `page_token` and `order_by` control paging and order; each response's `next_page_token` fetches the next page.
- Read the error messages; they say what is missing or invalid.
- Please keep requests bounded with filters and reasonable page sizes.

## Raw data

The Lab API serves only the derived tables [xatu-cbt](https://github.com/ethpandaops/xatu-cbt) builds. The raw event tables they are built from are published by [xatu-data](https://github.com/ethpandaops/xatu-data) as public Parquet files, with no key.

- [xatu-data guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethpandaops/xatu-data/master/llms.txt): xatu-data's own llms.txt, linking its Parquet and ClickHouse guides.
- [Table config](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethpandaops/xatu-data/master/config.yaml): YAML whose `tables[]` lists every published table with its `database`, its `partitioning` (`type`, `column`, `interval`) and, under `networks`, the `from` and `to` of the files published for each network.
- Files: `https://data.ethpandaops.io/xatu/{network}/databases/{database}/{table}/` followed by `{YYYY}/{M}/{D}.parquet` for daily datetime partitions, `{YYYY}/{M}/{D}/{H}.parquet` for hourly ones, or `{interval}/{start}.parquet` for integer partitions, where `{start}` is a multiple of the interval. Month, day and hour have no leading zero. The host has no directory listing and no wildcards, so build each URL from the config.
- Schemas: `schema/clickhouse/{database}/{table}.sql` in xatu-data holds each table's `CREATE TABLE` statement with column comments, dumped from the live ClickHouse.
- Migrations: the raw tables are created by the ClickHouse migrations in [xatu](https://github.com/ethpandaops/xatu/tree/master/deploy/migrations/clickhouse), and the derived tables by the migrations in [xatu-cbt](https://github.com/ethpandaops/xatu-cbt/tree/master/migrations).

## More

- [panda](https://github.com/ethpandaops/panda): ethPandaOps' CLI and MCP server for querying the underlying ClickHouse, Prometheus and Loki data directly, beyond what the Lab API exposes.
- [Source](https://github.com/ethpandaops/lab): the Lab frontend. The API is served by [cbt-api](https://github.com/ethpandaops/cbt-api) through [lab-backend](https://github.com/ethpandaops/lab-backend).
